title: Onprem customer journey notes — May 2025
content:
Context:
Customer: CortexHealth (large enterprise, multi-AZ onprem), rollout window May 12–16. Goal: zero-downtime cutover for inference workers behind customer LB, KMS integration for model keys, and 10ms p99 internal inference latency for short prompts. This doc is a running field-journal of the week, captured after standups and ad-hoc triage calls.

Attendees (drift between calls):
- Priya (owner)
- Diego (networking lead)
- Morgan (runtime/inference)
- Samira (customer success / onsite liaison)
- Customer SRE: Ajay / Lina
- Field engineer: Tom

Meeting objective (daily):
- Keep deploy on schedule, track unresolved customer blockers, capture debugging steps & handoffs.

Day 0 (preflight, May 12):
- Checklist run: inventory HW, OS images, driver versions, NVidia driver 525.x present; CUDA 11.8 verified.
- KMS smoke: test encrypt/decrypt using their HSM wrapper; succeeded on local test key but failed when using production key due to IP allowlist.
  - Root cause: customer firewall only allowed specific control-plane IPs; field engineer to request temporary whitelist for 3 control-plane addresses.
- Network baseline: MTU mismatch observed between rack switch and server (9000 vs 1500) which caused large packet fragmentation for KV cache sync tests.
  - Workaround: set instance-level MTU to 9000 on all inference nodes; customer network team to update switch config in maintenance window.

Day 1 (initial install, May 13):
- Router/BGP: transient route flaps during node reboots (seen in customer telemetry).
  - Diego set BGP hold-time to 60s and updated graceful-restart policy. Monitoring shows no further flaps in 2 hours.
- Certificate rotation: customer uses internal PKI; CRL lookup failing intermittently (timeouts).
  - Temporary: extended TLS handshake timeout in agent from 5s -> 20s. Long-term: customer to add CRL responder endpoints to route table.
- GPU affinity: observed uneven worker-to-GPU assignment under kube-scheduler with topology-aware hints reset.
  - Morgan patched node kubelet flags to respect alpha topology plugin; PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-config/pull/212

Day 2 (latency testing & ramp, May 14):
- Latency: p50 within target, but p99 ~22ms (target 10ms). Investigations:
  - KV cache misses spike on cold starts; spikes correlate with short 5–8 token prompts.
  - Observed frequent small batches leading to overhead on runtime startup path.
- Actions taken:
  - Enabled local prefix caching for customer workload (reduced p99 by ~6ms).
  - Adjusted batching: increased per-worker batch window from 2ms -> 6ms for non-interactive route (tradeoff: slightly higher p50 for batch jobs).

Day 3 (handoff & unresolved items, May 15):
- Unresolved Blockers:
  1) HSM IP allowlist (blocking production KMS usage). Status: customer security to open access window; field awaiting confirmation. Owner: Ajay (customer) / Samira to chase.
  2) Intermittent DNS timeouts affecting certificate revocation checks (CRL). Owner: Tom + customer network.
  3) Occasional inference worker OOMs when model autoload happens with simultaneous cache priming. Observed on node-07. Owner: Morgan.
- Customer feedback: happy with deterministic rollback path and canary routing. They asked for an explicit SLA doc for onprem installs (we promised a one-pager by EOD May 16).

Diagnostics & notes (free-form):
- Collected artifacts: systemd journal, nvidia-smi logs, kubelet logs from node-07 (see linked_artifacts). Tarball stored on S3: s3://redwood-field/cortexhealth/may-2025/node-07-diagnostics.tar.gz (customer-access controlled).
- Short commands used during triage:
  - check mem: free -h; ps aux --sort=-rss | head -n 10
  - nv driver: nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY, GPU
  - network perf: iperf3 -c x.x.x.x -P 8 -t 30
- Observed an application-level memory leak in a custom customer preprocessor that spikes during high-concurrency priming. Not our runtime; discussed mitigation: move preprocessor to sidecar and limit threads.

Risk assessment:
- If HSM access not opened within 48h, we must fallback to local-encrypted keys (customer risk: regulatory constraints). Escalation path: field eng -> infra security -> customer security lead.
- If DNS/CRL timeouts continue, risk to certificate validity checks leading to degraded TLS sessions for the control plane. Mitigation: local CRL cache (short TTL) implemented as interim patch.

Action items (explicit):
- Samira: confirm HSM whitelist window with customer security and post update in #field-cortex by EOD 2025-05-15. (status: pending)
- Diego: apply MTU switch update during maintenance; coordinate 2-hour maintenance window May 16 02:00–04:00 UTC. (status: scheduled)
- Morgan: root-cause OOM on node-07 — add cgroup memory cap, investigate model autoload concurrency. Deliver PR with conservative caps by 2025-05-17. (status: in_progress)
- Priya: draft onprem SLA one-pager and canary/rollback checklist; share with legal & solutions by 2025-05-16. (status: in_progress)
- Tom: deploy local CRL cache patch to control-plane agents; monitor for 24h. (status: deployed test)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Customer asked: can we support HSM fallback where only model keys are encrypted in customer HSM while control-plane stays in our hosted KMS? Need legal + security review. (Priya -> security)
- Are there any post-install telemetry metrics we should add to default hosted dashboards for onprem customers? Proposal: GPU utilization by model, cache hit ratio by request fingerprint, TLS handshake latencies. (to discuss in Tuesday ops sync)

Notes to self / field tips:
- Keep a short list of IP ranges to request for whitelist to speed HSM access (control-plane small set).
- If MTU mismatch suspected, first run: ip -s link show then small iperf with -M check.
- For certificate CRL issues, extending handshake timeout often buys time but hides root cause — insist on customer network fix.

Appendix (tickets & links):
- Linear: PL-834 (onprem HSM access flow)
- GH PR: ops-config PR #212 (kubelet topology flags)
- JIRA: JIRA-OPS-1987 (customer preprocessor memory leak)

Summary/next check-in:
- Next sync: May 16 10:00 UTC. Focus: confirm HSM access, verify MTU change post-maintenance, validate p99 target after local cache + batching changes.
- Overall sentiment: cautiously optimistic — major install path is complete, remaining items are network/security adjacent and require customer-side changes.

-- end of field journal entry --
